 Target heads into crucial holiday season with strong third-quarter sales

 Target's turnaround strategy may be gaining a foothold as the big-box chain enters the all-important holiday shopping season.
 The bullseye retailer reported its strongest quarter of sales growth in half a decade, CEO Michael Fiddelke said in a media briefing ahead of Target's third-quarter earnings report.
 Third-quarter net sales grew 7.1% to $27.1 billion, with comparable sales up 5.6%, ahead of analysts' expectations.
 Almost all of the comparable sales gains were driven by increased traffic, as shoppers responded positively to Target's improved merchandise, shopping experience, and value proposition, Fiddelke said.
 The company's performance in the quarter also benefited from hundreds of millions of dollars in investment in training and scheduling workers, which helped improve customer satisfaction scores and product availability, he said.
 Fiddelke also told Business Insider the company's new Ask Target AI shopping assistant is already having an impact on sales, with shoppers who use the tool completing purchases at more than twice the rate they did before it launched.
 In terms of merchandise categories, the results so far suggest that the areas where Target has chosen to focus its energy and attention are seeing growth, while others like home goods and apparel have yet to turn the corner.
 "We've got momentum in parts of each of those categories, and we need more," Fiddelke said.

 Dominick Reuter is a senior retail reporter for Business Insider, primarily covering Walmart, Target, Costco, and other big box retailers. His stories tend to focus on issues and trends that affect employees and customers, such as affordability challenges and the growing race to provide ultra-fast delivery services on e-commerce orders. Prior to joining BI in 2019, Dominick worked for more than a decade as an independent photojournalist covering a wide range of stories for global wire services and newspapers, including Reuters, the Wall Street Journal, and Agence France-Presse. Dominick studied photojournalism at Boston University and later earned a Masters in business and economics journalism from Columbia University.
